question: How can we systematically discover novel drug indications from existing compounds?
description: Finding unexpected therapeutic connections through mechanism-based inference
key_contradictions: Metformin shows benefits in cancer, aging, and neurodegeneration despite different mechanisms
Statins have CNS effects despite poor blood-brain barrier penetration
Why do anti-inflammatory drugs work in some CNS diseases but not others?

benchmark_hypotheses.statement: The pleiotropic effects of metformin across aging, cancer, and neurodegeneration are mediated by a fundamental energy sensing mechanism that converges on mitochondrial stress response through an unknown mitohormetic signaling pathway.

What if the CNS effects of statins are not due to direct brain penetration but to a peripheral signaling cascade that crosses the blood-brain barrier through a transcytosis mechanism involving lipid rafts?

Anti-inflammatory efficacy in CNS diseases is not determined by COX inhibition but by a threshold effect in microglial priming states that respond only when the intervention hits a specific nodal point in the neuroinflammatory network.
